title: Cohomology of a derived base-change map
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and $g':X'\to X$. Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, placed in degree zero in the bounded below derived category. For $q\in\mathbf Z$, under the canonical identifications
$$
\mathcal H^q(g^{-1}Rf_*F)\cong g^{-1}R^qf_*F,\qquad
\mathcal H^q(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F)=R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F,
$$
from [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], the map $\mathcal H^q(\Ex_{\square,F})$ of the derived exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is the usual higher-direct-image base-change map
$$
g^{-1}R^qf_*F\longrightarrow R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F.
$$
Here the usual map is the injective-resolution construction extending the underived exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]: apply that exchange termwise to a resolution of $F$, compare its $g'^{-1}$-pullback with a resolution on $X'$, and take degree-$q$ cohomology. For negative $q$ both higher direct images are zero. All coefficients in this statement are abelian groups.

proof.text: Use the supplied bounded below representatives I and J, source isomorphism s, and comparison j. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], the right-derived unit for f_* at I is invertible. The composite t = Q(j) composed with the inverse-image comparison and g'^{-1}(s) is invertible because all three factors are. No resolution is chosen and no injectivity of g'^{-1}I is used.

Apply the already proved bounded resolution factorization [lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-replacement] to I. Naturality of the derived exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] along s^{-1} transports this equation to F[0]. Naturality of the right-derived unit [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] along j identifies Q(f'_*(j)) followed by the unit at J and Rf'_*(t^{-1}) with the unit at g'^{-1}I followed by Rf'_*(phi^{-1} composed with g'^{-1}(s^{-1})). This follows by cancelling Q(j) against its factor in t. Cancel the invertible source comparison to obtain exactly the displayed resolution equation before cohomology. The private Lean lemma resolution_exchange_formula proves this elementary categorical calculation for arbitrary functors and natural transformations.

Apply degree-q cohomology to the equation from step 2, precompose with the fixed exact inverse-image cohomology comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], and postcompose with Rf'_* applied to the single-functor comparison. Functoriality and associativity give precisely the first conjunct. The localized termwise underived exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] in the formula is the usual resolution recipe.

For q < 0 apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] with lower bound zero to f_* and F[0], and separately to f'_* and (g'^{-1}F)[0]. Single-degree objects are cohomologically nonnegative by the standard t-structure instance. These are exactly the two IsZero conclusions.
